## 1. Purpose

This module evaluates three GBLUP structures under the six simulated scenarios
and the cross-validation partitions defined previously:

- **GBLUP-A:** additive genomic effect;
- **GBLUP-AD:** additive and dominance genomic effects;
- **GBLUP-ADE:** additive, dominance, and additive-by-additive epistatic genomic
  effects.

Each model is evaluated on the same 25 outer held-out splits within each
scenario. The complete workload therefore contains

\[
6 \times 3 \times 25 = 450
\]

scenario-by-model-by-split fits.

The analysis follows the same information separation used in the original
GBLUP-ADE benchmark:

- phenotype is the fitting response;
- phenotype values from the 200 outer-assessment individuals are hidden before
  fitting;
- genotypes from all 1,000 individuals are available for construction of the
  genomic relationship matrices;
- true genetic value is used only after prediction as the primary evaluation
  target.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

dir.create(
  "output/simulated/m03/figures",
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)
```

## 2. Packages and inputs

### 2.1 Packages

The code uses `knitr` to format tables; `ggplot2` and `ggthemes` for figures;
`sommer` for genomic relationship matrices and mixed models; and `foreach`
with `doParallel` for parallel model fitting.

```{r packages, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(sommer)
library(foreach)
library(doParallel)
```

### 2.2 Input data

The phenotype and simulated true genetic-value matrices contain the six
scenarios in columns. The genotype matrix contains individuals in rows, with
consistent identifiers assigned to its rows. The outer validation partitions
identify which individuals contribute phenotypes to fitting and which are held
out for prediction.

```{r inputs}
# Load the simulated population and common cross-validation design.
common <- readRDS(
  "output/simulated/audit/preprocessed_simulated_common.rds"
)

cv <- readRDS(
  "output/simulated/validation/simulated_cv_design.rds"
)

# Separate fitting responses, evaluation targets, and marker information.
phenotype <- common$phenotype
true_g <- common$true_genetic_value
geno <- common$genotype_m101

# Assign a consistent individual order to genotype rows and model effects.
ids <- seq_len(
  nrow(geno)
)

id_labels <- sprintf(
  "ID%04d",
  ids
)

rownames(geno) <- id_labels

scenario_names <- colnames(phenotype)

model_names <- c(
  "GBLUP_A",
  "GBLUP_AD",
  "GBLUP_ADE"
)

# Summarize the dimensions and statistical roles of the input objects.
input_summary <- data.frame(
  Object = c(
    "Phenotype",
    "True genetic value",
    "Genotype",
    "Outer validation splits"
  ),
  Structure = c(
    paste(dim(phenotype), collapse = " x "),
    paste(dim(true_g), collapse = " x "),
    paste(dim(geno), collapse = " x "),
    length(cv$outer_splits)
  ),
  Role = c(
    "Response used for model fitting.",
    "Primary held-out evaluation target.",
    "Marker information used to construct the genomic relationship matrices.",
    "Common outer cross-validation partitions for all models."
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Objects entering the simulated GBLUP analysis",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The data contain 1,000 aligned individuals and six simulation scenarios. Every
outer split contains 800 analysis individuals and 200 assessment individuals.
Each individual is assessed once per repetition, giving five held-out
predictions per scenario and model across five cross-validation repetitions.

## 3. GBLUP models

### 3.1 GBLUP-A

The additive model is

\[
\mathbf{y}
=
\mathbf{1}\mu
+
\mathbf{a}
+
\boldsymbol{\varepsilon},
\]

with

\[
\mathbf{a}
\sim
N(0,\mathbf{A}\sigma_a^2).
\]

### 3.2 GBLUP-AD

The additive-dominance model is

\[
\mathbf{y}
=
\mathbf{1}\mu
+
\mathbf{a}
+
\mathbf{d}
+
\boldsymbol{\varepsilon},
\]

with

\[
\mathbf{d}
\sim
N(0,\mathbf{D}\sigma_d^2).
\]

### 3.3 GBLUP-ADE

The third structure extends GBLUP-AD with the additive-by-additive epistatic
effect:

\[
\mathbf{y}
=
\mathbf{1}\mu
+
\mathbf{a}
+
\mathbf{d}
+
\mathbf{e}
+
\boldsymbol{\varepsilon},
\]

where

\[
\mathbf{e}
\sim
N(0,\mathbf{E}\sigma_e^2).
\]

The residual term in all three models is

\[
\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}
\sim
N(0,\mathbf{I}\sigma_\varepsilon^2).
\]

### 3.4 Genomic relationship matrices

```{r relationship-matrix-roles}
# Associate each GBLUP structure with its genomic covariance components.
relationship_matrices <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "GBLUP-A",
    "GBLUP-AD",
    "GBLUP-ADE"
  ),
  Matrices = c(
    "A",
    "A + D",
    "A + D + E"
  ),
  Genetic_effects = c(
    "Additive",
    "Additive + dominance",
    "Additive + dominance + epistasis"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

relationship_matrices |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Genomic components represented by the three GBLUP models",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

Matrix A describes additive genomic covariance, D describes dominance genomic
covariance, and E represents the second-order additive-by-additive relationship
used in the ADE model. These matrices depend only on marker information and do
not use phenotype or true genetic value.

The additive (A), dominance (D), and additive-by-additive epistatic (E)
relationship matrices are constructed from marker genotypes. They have the
same individual ordering and are used consistently across all scenarios and
validation partitions. Their summaries describe matrix dimensions, symmetry,
finite entries, and mean diagonal values.

```{r genomic-kernels, eval=FALSE}
# Construct additive, dominance, and additive-by-additive genomic kernels.
A_matrix <- sommer::A.mat(
  geno,
  min.MAF = 0
)

D_matrix <- sommer::D.mat(
  geno,
  nishio = TRUE,
  min.MAF = 0
)

E_matrix <- sommer::E.mat(
  geno,
  nishio = TRUE,
  type = "A#A",
  min.MAF = 0
)

# Align rows and columns across all three matrices by individual.
rownames(A_matrix) <- id_labels
colnames(A_matrix) <- id_labels

rownames(D_matrix) <- id_labels
colnames(D_matrix) <- id_labels

rownames(E_matrix) <- id_labels
colnames(E_matrix) <- id_labels

# Describe dimensions, symmetry, finite entries, and mean diagonals.
kernel_summary <- data.frame(
  Kernel = c(
    "Additive",
    "Dominance",
    "Epistatic"
  ),
  Rows = c(
    nrow(A_matrix),
    nrow(D_matrix),
    nrow(E_matrix)
  ),
  Columns = c(
    ncol(A_matrix),
    ncol(D_matrix),
    ncol(E_matrix)
  ),
  Symmetric = c(
    isTRUE(
      all.equal(
        A_matrix,
        t(A_matrix),
        tolerance = 1e-8
      )
    ),
    isTRUE(
      all.equal(
        D_matrix,
        t(D_matrix),
        tolerance = 1e-8
      )
    ),
    isTRUE(
      all.equal(
        E_matrix,
        t(E_matrix),
        tolerance = 1e-8
      )
    )
  ),
  Finite = c(
    all(is.finite(A_matrix)),
    all(is.finite(D_matrix)),
    all(is.finite(E_matrix))
  ),
  Mean_diagonal = c(
    mean(diag(A_matrix)),
    mean(diag(D_matrix)),
    mean(diag(E_matrix))
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dir.create(
  "output/simulated/gblup",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# Store the relationship-matrix summary.
write.csv(
  kernel_summary,
  "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_kernel_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

The relationship matrices are summarized by their dimensions, symmetry,
finite-valued entries, and mean diagonal values.

```{r kernel-summary}
# Retrieve the relationship-matrix summary for presentation.
kernel_summary <- read.csv(
  "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_kernel_summary.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

kernel_summary[
  ,
  c(
    "Kernel",
    "Rows",
    "Columns",
    "Symmetric",
    "Finite",
    "Mean_diagonal"
  )
] |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Genomic relationship matrices used by the GBLUP models",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 4. Held-out prediction

For every scenario, model, and outer split, the 200 assessment phenotypes are
replaced by `NA` before model fitting. The fitted model then predicts those
individuals from the available genomic information.

The GEBV is stored on the original trait scale and includes the fitted
intercept together with the genomic effects represented by the corresponding
model:

\[
\widehat{\mathrm{GEBV}}_{\mathrm{A}}
=
\widehat{\mu}
+
\widehat{a},
\]

\[
\widehat{\mathrm{GEBV}}_{\mathrm{AD}}
=
\widehat{\mu}
+
\widehat{a}
+
\widehat{d},
\]

and

\[
\widehat{\mathrm{GEBV}}_{\mathrm{ADE}}
=
\widehat{\mu}
+
\widehat{a}
+
\widehat{d}
+
\widehat{e}.
\]

True genetic values are accessed only after the held-out GEBVs have been
obtained.

## 5. Model fitting

The three models use a common fixed intercept and residual variance, while
the random-effect structure progressively includes additive, dominance, and
epistatic genomic components. In `sommer::mmes()`, `Gu` supplies the relevant
relationship matrix. Each fit allows 50 iterations and uses a log-likelihood
parameter convergence tolerance of `1e-4`. For a given scenario and outer
partition, the three specifications are:

```{r model-calls, eval=FALSE}
# GBLUP-A: use the additive covariance matrix only.
fit_A <- sommer::mmes(
  y ~ 1,
  random = ~
    vsm(
      ism(id),
      Gu = A_matrix
    ),
  rcov = ~ units,
  nIters = 50L,
  tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
  data = dat,
  verbose = FALSE,
  dateWarning = FALSE
)

# GBLUP-AD: add the dominance covariance matrix.
fit_AD <- sommer::mmes(
  y ~ 1,
  random = ~
    vsm(
      ism(id),
      Gu = A_matrix
    ) +
    vsm(
      ism(idd),
      Gu = D_matrix
    ),
  rcov = ~ units,
  nIters = 50L,
  tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
  data = dat,
  verbose = FALSE,
  dateWarning = FALSE
)

# GBLUP-ADE: also include additive-by-additive epistasis.
fit_ADE <- sommer::mmes(
  y ~ 1,
  random = ~
    vsm(
      ism(id),
      Gu = A_matrix
    ) +
    vsm(
      ism(idd),
      Gu = D_matrix
    ) +
    vsm(
      ism(ide),
      Gu = E_matrix
    ),
  rcov = ~ units,
  nIters = 50L,
  tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
  data = dat,
  verbose = FALSE,
  dateWarning = FALSE
)
```

For each of the six scenarios, the three model structures are paired with all
25 outer splits, producing 450 fitting tasks. The task identifiers retain the
scenario, model, repetition, fold, and partition so predictions can be compared
for exactly the same assessment individuals.

```{r task-table}
# Name the three genomic structures for the simulation study.
structures <- c(
  "A",
  "AD",
  "ADE"
)

# Read unique outer-fold identifiers from the shared validation design.
outer_meta <- unique(
  cv$outer_assignments[
    ,
    c(
      "Repetition",
      "OuterFold",
      "SplitID"
    )
  ]
)

outer_meta <- outer_meta[
  order(
    outer_meta$Repetition,
    outer_meta$OuterFold
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Form every scenario-by-model combination.
task_table <- merge(
  data.frame(
    Scenario = scenario_names,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  data.frame(
    Structure = structures,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  by = NULL
)

task_table <- merge(
  task_table,
  outer_meta,
  by = NULL
)

# Label each model and arrange tasks in a reproducible order.
task_table$Model <- paste0(
  "GBLUP_",
  task_table$Structure
)

task_table <- task_table[
  order(
    match(
      task_table$Scenario,
      scenario_names
    ),
    match(
      task_table$Structure,
      structures
    ),
    task_table$Repetition,
    task_table$OuterFold
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Identify each scenario, model, and outer assessment partition.
task_table$TaskID <- paste(
  task_table$Scenario,
  task_table$Model,
  task_table$SplitID,
  sep = "_"
)

rownames(task_table) <- NULL

```

Each task first identifies its training and assessment individuals. All marker
genotypes remain available for genomic covariance calculations, but phenotypes
from the 200 assessment individuals are masked before fitting. The model is
fitted using the 800 remaining phenotypes, and GEBVs are constructed from the
intercept and the relevant genomic effects. Held-out predictions are then
compared with simulated true genetic values and observed phenotypes to obtain
split-level performance metrics. The individual predictions are retained for
subsequent comparisons, with independent fits distributed across workers.

```{r fit-all-gblup-models, eval=FALSE}
# Choose a practical parallel-worker count from the available CPU cores.
logical_cores <- parallel::detectCores(
  logical = TRUE
)

if (is.na(logical_cores)) {
  logical_cores <- 2L
}

default_workers <- max(
  1L,
  min(
    10L,
    floor(logical_cores / 2L),
    max(
      1L,
      logical_cores - 2L
    )
  )
)

# Allow a user-specified worker count without changing model specifications.
requested_workers <- suppressWarnings(
  as.integer(
    Sys.getenv(
      "GBLUP_WORKERS",
      ""
    )
  )
)

if (
  is.na(requested_workers) ||
  requested_workers < 1L
) {
  N_WORKERS <- default_workers
} else {
  N_WORKERS <- min(
    requested_workers,
    max(
      1L,
      logical_cores - 2L
    )
  )
}

# Retain QTL counts and nominal heritability for scenario annotations.
control <- common$scenario_control

# Create the parallel backend and initialize package libraries on workers.
cluster <- parallel::makeCluster(
  N_WORKERS
)

worker_libpaths <- .libPaths()

parallel::clusterExport(
  cluster,
  "worker_libpaths",
  envir = environment()
)

parallel::clusterEvalQ(
  cluster,
  {
    .libPaths(
      worker_libpaths
    )

    library(foreach)
    library(doParallel)
    library(sommer)

    NULL
  }
)

# Register the cluster as the backend for parallel fitting.
doParallel::registerDoParallel(
  cluster
)

# Evaluate each independent scenario-model-split task.
parallel_results <-
  foreach::foreach(
    i = seq_len(
      nrow(task_table)
    ),
    .packages = "sommer",
    .inorder = TRUE,
    .errorhandling = "stop"
  ) %dopar% {

    # Recover the current scenario, GBLUP structure, and held-out split.
    task <- task_table[
      i,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    scenario <- task$Scenario
    structure <- task$Structure

    scenario_index <- match(
      scenario,
      scenario_names
    )

    split <- cv$outer_splits[[
      task$SplitID
    ]]

    # Identify training individuals and their assessment counterparts.
    analysis_index <- match(
      split$analysis_ids,
      ids
    )

    assessment_index <- match(
      split$assessment_ids,
      ids
    )

    phenotype_vector <- phenotype[
      ,
      scenario_index
    ]

    id_factor <- factor(
      id_labels,
      levels = id_labels
    )

    # Assemble the phenotypic response and individual incidence factors.
    dat <- data.frame(
      y = phenotype_vector,
      id = id_factor,
      idd = id_factor,
      ide = id_factor
    )

    # Mask assessment phenotypes to prevent leakage into model fitting.
    dat$y[
      assessment_index
    ] <- NA_real_

    # Fit the selected model using only the 800 available phenotypes.
    fit_start <- proc.time()[[
      "elapsed"
    ]]

    # Additive model: only the additive genomic effect enters the fit.
    if (structure == "A") {

      fit <- sommer::mmes(
        y ~ 1,
        random = ~
          vsm(
            ism(id),
            Gu = A_matrix
          ),
        rcov = ~ units,
        nIters = 50L,
        tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
        data = dat,
        verbose = FALSE,
        dateWarning = FALSE
      )

    } else if (structure == "AD") {

      # Additive-dominance model: include both genetic components.
      fit <- sommer::mmes(
        y ~ 1,
        random = ~
          vsm(
            ism(id),
            Gu = A_matrix
          ) +
          vsm(
            ism(idd),
            Gu = D_matrix
          ),
        rcov = ~ units,
        nIters = 50L,
        tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
        data = dat,
        verbose = FALSE,
        dateWarning = FALSE
      )

    } else {

      # Full ADE model: include additive, dominance, and epistatic effects.
      fit <- sommer::mmes(
        y ~ 1,
        random = ~
          vsm(
            ism(id),
            Gu = A_matrix
          ) +
          vsm(
            ism(idd),
            Gu = D_matrix
          ) +
          vsm(
            ism(ide),
            Gu = E_matrix
          ),
        rcov = ~ units,
        nIters = 50L,
        tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
        data = dat,
        verbose = FALSE,
        dateWarning = FALSE
      )
    }

    fit_seconds <-
      proc.time()[[
        "elapsed"
      ]] -
      fit_start

    # Recover random-effect predictions and assemble GEBVs.
    prediction_start <- proc.time()[[
      "elapsed"
    ]]

    additive <- rep(
      0,
      length(ids)
    )

    dominance <- rep(
      0,
      length(ids)
    )

    epistatic <- rep(
      0,
      length(ids)
    )

    # Project estimated additive effects to individual-specific values.
    additive_effect <- as.matrix(
      fit$uList[[
        "vsm(ism(id), Gu = A_matrix)"
      ]]
    )

    additive_incidence <- model.matrix(
      ~ id - 1,
      data = dat
    )

    additive <- as.numeric(
      additive_incidence %*%
        additive_effect[
          ,
          1L,
          drop = FALSE
        ]
    )

    # Dominance contributes only to AD and ADE predictions.
    if (
      structure == "AD" ||
      structure == "ADE"
    ) {

      dominance_effect <- as.matrix(
        fit$uList[[
          "vsm(ism(idd), Gu = D_matrix)"
        ]]
      )

      dominance_incidence <- model.matrix(
        ~ idd - 1,
        data = dat
      )

      dominance <- as.numeric(
        dominance_incidence %*%
          dominance_effect[
            ,
            1L,
            drop = FALSE
          ]
      )
    }

    # Add epistatic predictions only for the ADE structure.
    if (structure == "ADE") {

      epistatic_effect <- as.matrix(
        fit$uList[[
          "vsm(ism(ide), Gu = E_matrix)"
        ]]
      )

      epistatic_incidence <- model.matrix(
        ~ ide - 1,
        data = dat
      )

      epistatic <- as.numeric(
        epistatic_incidence %*%
          epistatic_effect[
            ,
            1L,
            drop = FALSE
          ]
      )
    }

    # Sum genetic effects and add the fitted intercept on the trait scale.
    genomic_component <-
      additive +
      dominance +
      epistatic

    intercept <- as.numeric(
      fit$b
    )[
      1L
    ]

    gebv <-
      intercept +
      genomic_component

    predict_seconds <-
      proc.time()[[
        "elapsed"
      ]] -
      prediction_start

    # Extract outcomes for the held-out assessment individuals only.
    observed_test <- phenotype_vector[
      assessment_index
    ]

    true_g_test <- true_g[
      assessment_index,
      scenario_index
    ]

    gebv_test <- gebv[
      assessment_index
    ]

    # Primary assessment: agreement with the known simulated genetic values.
    genetic_pearson <- cor(
      gebv_test,
      true_g_test,
      method = "pearson"
    )

    genetic_spearman <- cor(
      gebv_test,
      true_g_test,
      method = "spearman"
    )

    genetic_rmse <- sqrt(
      mean(
        (
          gebv_test -
          true_g_test
        )^2
      )
    )

    genetic_mae <- mean(
      abs(
        gebv_test -
        true_g_test
      )
    )

    genetic_bias <- mean(
      gebv_test -
        true_g_test
    )

    genetic_slope <- as.numeric(
      coef(
        lm(
          true_g_test ~ gebv_test
        )
      )[2L]
    )

    # Secondary assessment: agreement with the observed phenotypes.
    phenotype_pearson <- cor(
      gebv_test,
      observed_test,
      method = "pearson"
    )

    phenotype_spearman <- cor(
      gebv_test,
      observed_test,
      method = "spearman"
    )

    phenotype_rmse <- sqrt(
      mean(
        (
          gebv_test -
          observed_test
        )^2
      )
    )

    phenotype_mae <- mean(
      abs(
        gebv_test -
        observed_test
      )
    )

    phenotype_bias <- mean(
      gebv_test -
        observed_test
    )

    phenotype_slope <- as.numeric(
      coef(
        lm(
          observed_test ~ gebv_test
        )
      )[2L]
    )

    # Associate each fit with its simulation characteristics.
    meta <- control[
      control$Scenario == scenario,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    # Store one row of performance metrics per fitted task.
    result_row <- data.frame(
      Dataset = "simulated",
      Scenario = scenario,
      QTL_N = meta$QTL_N,
      H2_nominal = meta$H2_nominal,
      Repetition = task$Repetition,
      Fold = task$OuterFold,
      SplitID = task$SplitID,
      TaskID = task$TaskID,
      Model = task$Model,
      Structure = structure,
      N_train = length(
        analysis_index
      ),
      N_test = length(
        assessment_index
      ),
      Genetic_Pearson =
        genetic_pearson,
      Genetic_Spearman =
        genetic_spearman,
      Genetic_RMSE =
        genetic_rmse,
      Genetic_MAE =
        genetic_mae,
      Genetic_Bias =
        genetic_bias,
      Genetic_Slope =
        genetic_slope,
      Phenotype_Pearson =
        phenotype_pearson,
      Phenotype_Spearman =
        phenotype_spearman,
      Phenotype_RMSE =
        phenotype_rmse,
      Phenotype_MAE =
        phenotype_mae,
      Phenotype_Bias =
        phenotype_bias,
      Phenotype_Slope =
        phenotype_slope,
      Fit_seconds =
        fit_seconds,
      Predict_seconds =
        predict_seconds,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    # Store 200 held-out predictions and their additive/AD/ADE components.
    prediction_rows <- data.frame(
      Dataset = "simulated",
      Scenario = scenario,
      QTL_N = meta$QTL_N,
      H2_nominal = meta$H2_nominal,
      Repetition = task$Repetition,
      Fold = task$OuterFold,
      SplitID = task$SplitID,
      TaskID = task$TaskID,
      Model = task$Model,
      Structure = structure,
      ID = ids[
        assessment_index
      ],
      Observed_Phenotype =
        observed_test,
      True_Genetic_Value =
        true_g_test,
      GEBV =
        gebv_test,
      Additive_Prediction =
        additive[
          assessment_index
        ],
      Dominance_Prediction =
        dominance[
          assessment_index
        ],
      Epistatic_Prediction =
        epistatic[
          assessment_index
        ],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    list(
      result = result_row,
      predictions = prediction_rows
    )
  }

# Release parallel workers after completing all tasks.
parallel::stopCluster(
  cluster
)

# Combine split-level summaries and individual predictions in task order.
result_list <- vector(
  "list",
  length(parallel_results)
)

prediction_list <- vector(
  "list",
  length(parallel_results)
)

for (
  i in
    seq_along(parallel_results)
) {

  result_list[[i]] <-
    parallel_results[[i]]$result

  prediction_list[[i]] <-
    parallel_results[[i]]$predictions
}

# Bind all fitting results into a single table.
results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  result_list
)

predictions <- do.call(
  rbind,
  prediction_list
)

rownames(results) <- NULL
rownames(predictions) <- NULL

# Save fit-level results and held-out predictions for subsequent analyses.
dir.create(
  "output/simulated/gblup",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  results,
  "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_results.rds",
  compress = "gzip"
)

write.csv(
  results,
  "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  predictions,
  "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_predictions.rds",
  compress = "gzip"
)

write.csv(
  predictions,
  "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_predictions.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

The numbers of completed fits by scenario and model are summarized below.
Each combination comprises five outer folds repeated five times.

```{r task-summary}
# Read the fit-level results before summarizing counts.
results <- readRDS(
  "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_results.rds"
)

results$Model <- factor(
  results$Model,
  levels = model_names
)


# Tabulate completed fits for each scenario and model.
task_summary <- as.data.frame(
  table(
    results$Scenario,
    results$Model
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

names(task_summary) <- c(
  "Scenario",
  "Model",
  "Fits"
)

task_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Number of outer GBLUP fits by scenario and model",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 6. Evaluation metrics

The **true genetic value** is the primary target because it is known in the
simulation and directly measures recovery of the simulated genetic signal.

The **phenotype** is retained as a secondary target because it includes the
genetic signal together with residual variation.

Held-out predictive performance is summarized using the following metrics:

- **Pearson correlation:** linear association between GEBV and the target;
- **Spearman correlation:** rank association between GEBV and the target;
- **RMSE:** prediction error on the original scale;
- **MAE:** mean absolute prediction error on the original scale.

Bias and calibration slope are complementary measures. Bias is
`mean(prediction - target)`, and calibration slope is the coefficient of
prediction in `lm(target ~ prediction)`. R-squared is not used.

No evaluation target is used during model fitting.

## 7. Predictive performance

### 7.1 True genetic value

Mean predictive performance is computed across the 25 outer assessment splits
within each scenario and GBLUP structure.

```{r genetic-performance-summary}
# Average genetic-value prediction metrics within scenario-model groups.
genetic_performance <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    Genetic_Pearson,
    Genetic_Spearman,
    Genetic_RMSE,
    Genetic_MAE,
    Genetic_Bias,
    Genetic_Slope
  ) ~ Scenario + Model,
  data = results,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

genetic_performance <- genetic_performance[
  order(
    match(
      genetic_performance$Scenario,
      scenario_names
    ),
    match(
      as.character(
        genetic_performance$Model
      ),
      model_names
    )
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

genetic_performance |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Primary evaluation against true genetic value",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The scenario sequence represents the predefined simulation settings. Because
the simulation factors change jointly across scenarios, differences among C1-C6
should be interpreted as differences among the complete scenarios rather than
as isolated effects of one parameter.

### 7.2 Phenotype

The same aggregation is repeated using observed phenotype as the secondary
prediction target.

```{r phenotype-performance-summary}
# Average observed-phenotype metrics within scenario-model groups.
phenotype_performance <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    Phenotype_Pearson,
    Phenotype_Spearman,
    Phenotype_RMSE,
    Phenotype_MAE,
    Phenotype_Bias,
    Phenotype_Slope
  ) ~ Scenario + Model,
  data = results,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

phenotype_performance <- phenotype_performance[
  order(
    match(
      phenotype_performance$Scenario,
      scenario_names
    ),
    match(
      as.character(
        phenotype_performance$Model
      ),
      model_names
    )
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

phenotype_performance |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Secondary evaluation against phenotype",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

### 7.3 Performance across outer splits

Boxplots show the variation in held-out Pearson correlations with true genetic
value across repetitions and outer folds for each model.

```{r genetic-correlation-figure, fig.cap="Held-out Pearson correlation between GEBV and true genetic value across the 25 outer splits for GBLUP-A, GBLUP-AD, and GBLUP-ADE."}
# Visualize held-out genetic-value correlations across outer splits.
p_genetic_correlation <- ggplot(
  results,
  aes(
    x = Scenario,
    y = Genetic_Pearson,
    fill = Model
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.72,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.75,
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.8
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_gdocs(
    labels = c(
      "GBLUP-A",
      "GBLUP-AD",
      "GBLUP-ADE"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Simulation scenario",
    y = "Pearson correlation with true genetic value",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gdocs()

print(
  p_genetic_correlation
)
```

```{r save-genetic-correlation-tiff, include=FALSE}
ggsave(
  "output/simulated/m03/figures/gblup_genetic_correlation_by_scenario.tiff",
  plot = p_genetic_correlation,
  device = "tiff",
  width = 8.5,
  height = 5.5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```

The corresponding RMSE distributions describe prediction errors on the
original trait scale for each scenario and model.

```{r genetic-rmse-figure, fig.cap="Held-out RMSE for true genetic value across the 25 outer splits for GBLUP-A, GBLUP-AD, and GBLUP-ADE."}
# Visualize held-out genetic-value RMSE across outer splits.
p_genetic_rmse <- ggplot(
  results,
  aes(
    x = Scenario,
    y = Genetic_RMSE,
    fill = Model
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.72,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.75,
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.8
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_gdocs(
    labels = c(
      "GBLUP-A",
      "GBLUP-AD",
      "GBLUP-ADE"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Simulation scenario",
    y = "RMSE for true genetic value",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gdocs()

print(
  p_genetic_rmse
)
```

```{r save-genetic-rmse-tiff, include=FALSE}
ggsave(
  "output/simulated/m03/figures/gblup_genetic_rmse_by_scenario.tiff",
  plot = p_genetic_rmse,
  device = "tiff",
  width = 8.5,
  height = 5.5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```

The boxplots summarize variation among the 25 held-out splits. They are
descriptive summaries of repeated cross-validation and are not treated as
independent inferential replicates.

## 8. Split-level variability

The same split-level results can be summarized numerically without introducing
additional model-selection criteria.

For each scenario and GBLUP structure, this summary reports the number of
held-out splits, descriptive statistics for correlations and errors, and the
observed range of Pearson correlations.

```{r split-summary}
# Initialize the descriptive split-level summary.
split_summary <- data.frame(
  Scenario = character(0),
  Model = character(0),
  N = integer(0),
  Pearson_mean = numeric(0),
  Pearson_sd = numeric(0),
  Pearson_min = numeric(0),
  Pearson_max = numeric(0),
  Spearman_mean = numeric(0),
  Spearman_sd = numeric(0),
  RMSE_mean = numeric(0),
  RMSE_sd = numeric(0),
  MAE_mean = numeric(0),
  MAE_sd = numeric(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Summarize the 25 held-out assessments for each scenario and model.
for (
  scenario in
    scenario_names
) {

  for (
    model_name in
      model_names
  ) {

    x <- results[
      results$Scenario == scenario &
        as.character(
          results$Model
        ) == model_name,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    split_summary <- rbind(
      split_summary,
      data.frame(
        Scenario = scenario,
        Model = model_name,
        N = nrow(x),
        Pearson_mean = mean(
          x$Genetic_Pearson,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Pearson_sd = sd(
          x$Genetic_Pearson,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Pearson_min = min(
          x$Genetic_Pearson,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Pearson_max = max(
          x$Genetic_Pearson,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Spearman_mean = mean(
          x$Genetic_Spearman,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Spearman_sd = sd(
          x$Genetic_Spearman,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        RMSE_mean = mean(
          x$Genetic_RMSE,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        RMSE_sd = sd(
          x$Genetic_RMSE,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        MAE_mean = mean(
          x$Genetic_MAE,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        MAE_sd = sd(
          x$Genetic_MAE,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )
  }
}

# Display the variability of genetic-value prediction across splits.
split_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "True genetic-value prediction across outer splits",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 9. Computational time

The genomic matrices are constructed once and reused across the complete
analysis. Model fitting is repeated for each scenario, model, and outer split.
The table below summarizes the mean fitting and prediction time per model.

```{r time-summary}
# Average elapsed fitting and prediction times by model.
time_summary <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    Fit_seconds,
    Predict_seconds
  ) ~ Model,
  data = results,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

time_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Mean computational time per GBLUP fit",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )


```

These times describe the completed computation on the machine used for the
analysis and should not be interpreted as hardware-independent characteristics
of the models.
